title: Code Editor does not properly work with some international keyboards on Linux (Ubuntu 24)
body:
### Tested versions

-  I do not have a windows machine at the moment, but last time i used it, I don't remember having issues.
-  reproducible on 4.4.1, 4.5, and 4.5.1 on Linux (two different Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS machines)


### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono - Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS 24.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti - AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 60.38 GiB memory

### Issue description

- I mostly use this keyboard layout on Ubuntu: English US International with Dead Keys. But I often need to switch my keyboard to the standard US layout when using Godot's Code editor. The code editor stops writing whenever I try to use any key that is used to insert accents, such as quotes. For example: to write the letter ´Ü´, I must press  ["] then [U]. Or if I want to write the actual " character, I need to press ["] then [SPACE]. However, the editor stops receiving any other input after I press ["] (which should have allowed me to write a letter with [¨] or just ["] with the next keypress).
- The following error pops up when trying to press the second character: 
-- ERROR: scene/gui/text_edit.cpp:6387 - Condition "p_column > text[p_line].length()" is true. Returning: 0

### Steps to reproduce

- Switch the Ubuntu 24 system to English US International with Dead Keys.
- Open the code editor
- Try to type quotes (by pressing ["] then [SPACE]).
- Note that nothing else is getting written even if you click on another line.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[new-game-project.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22954190/new-game-project.zip)

I have created one with one code file.
